evidence.field: 大部; PDF p. 922, printed p. 907; headword, form chart, explanation
evidence.text: The scan shows the 大部 section and headword 大 dà, followed by a chart labeled 商, 西周, 春秋, 战国, 秦, 《说文》小篆, 汉 and 楷书. The explanation calls 大 pictographic, describes the oracle-bone and bronze forms as a frontal person with arms extended and legs apart, proposes ‘adult’ as the original sense, and relates ‘big’ to it. This is the book’s analysis; its dated semantic sequence is not established by the passage. The entry continues onto PDF p. 923, which was not inspected in this invocation.
evidence.title: 字源, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社 / 遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.text: The entry interprets 大 as a frontal standing adult with arms hanging down, proposes ‘adult’ relative to child as an early sense from which ‘big’ developed, and cites bronze usage opposite 小. It also says 大 and 夫 were once one graph, later differentiated by adding a short stroke to 夫. Its arm-pose description differs from 字源’s; both accounts identify a human figure. The semantic development and 夫 account are source analyses, not independently established dated sequences here.

gaps: 字源 PDF p. 923 continues the 大 entry in provisional OCR, but that page’s scan was not supplied or inspected; continuation-only claims are excluded.

The book’s account on PDF p. 922, printed p. 907, describes the arms as extended; CUHK describes them as hanging down. The inspected Sinica record supports only a frontal human figure, so pose remains unsettled.
The exact earliest dated use meaning ‘adult’ or ‘big’ was not established. The adult-to-big semantic link remains a source analysis without a dated sequence of intermediate uses.
CUHK cites the bronze phrase 郘鐘「大鐘八聿(肆)」, but this research did not independently verify the primary inscription or vessel date.
Specific stroke-by-stroke development, possible corruption, and chronology of variants were not established by the inspected sources.
The official Unihan U+5927 lookup could not be accessed; the supplied local row is not external click-through evidence.
